competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency requires students to 'Distinguish even and odd numbers using division by 2.' The sample items directly and explicitly fulfill this requirement by evaluating parity through division by 2 or partitioning into 2 equal parts. For example, seed 501 assesses evenness via exact divisibility ('Dividing 82 by 2 gives an exact whole number, so 82 is an even number. True or False?'), seed 43 tests oddness via inexact division ('5 ÷ 2 does not come out exactly, so 5 is an odd number. True or False?'), and seed 46 tests evenness via equal sharing ('10 can be divided into 2 equal parts, so 10 is an even number. True or False?').

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items comprehensively cover the range of even and odd numbers across single-digit and 2-digit numbers up to within 100. Both true and false propositions are thoroughly tested across both odd and even categories. For instance, odd numbers are evaluated in seed 44 ('Dividing 53 by 2 does not give an exact whole number, so 53 is an odd number. True or False?'), seed 45 ('35 can be divided into 2 equal parts, so 35 is an even number. True or False?'), and seed 604 ('Dividing 9 by 2 gives an exact whole number, so 9 is an even number. True or False?'). Even numbers are evaluated in seed 46 ('10 can be divided into 2 equal parts, so 10 is an even number. True or False?') and seed 500 ('60 cannot be divided into 2 equal whole parts, so 60 is an odd number. True or False?').

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The linguistic complexity, vocabulary, and arithmetic demand are precisely calibrated for Grade 2 Quarter 3 learners. Phrasings such as 'can be divided into 2 equal parts' (seed 45: '35 can be divided into 2 equal parts, so 35 is an even number. True or False?') and 'does not come out exactly' (seed 602: '52 ÷ 2 does not come out exactly, so 52 is an odd number. True or False?') translate the concept of division by 2 into intuitive, grade-appropriate terms without introducing unneeded cognitive load or premature formal notation.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator exhibits healthy variety across item templates and syntactic structures. Variants include formal division symbol phrasing (seed 502: '65 ÷ 2 comes out exactly, so 65 is an even number. True or False?'), verbal division phrasing (seed 600: 'Dividing 34 by 2 does not give an exact whole number, so 34 is an odd number. True or False?'), and equal parts sharing phrasing (seed 601: '25 cannot be divided into 2 equal whole parts, so 25 is an odd number. True or False?'). This ensures students are evaluated on the underlying mathematical principle rather than pattern-matching a single sentence stem.

competency_alignment.rationale: All generated items align directly and strictly to the learning competency without scope drift or irrelevant operations. Every question hinges solely on the definition of even and odd numbers through division by 2. For instance, seed 605 ('Dividing 23 by 2 gives an exact whole number, so 23 is an even number. True or False?') tests the core relationship between divisibility by 2 and even/odd classification without distracting context.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical scale is fully appropriate for Grade 2 learners, testing single-digit integers (e.g., 5 in seed 43: '5 ÷ 2 does not come out exactly, so 5 is an odd number. True or False?', 9 in seed 604: 'Dividing 9 by 2 gives an exact whole number, so 9 is an even number. True or False?') and 2-digit integers under 100 (e.g., 10, 22, 23, 25, 34, 35, 52, 53, 60, 65, 82). These numbers provide a realistic range for Grade 2 students practicing divisibility by 2.
